## How a shift works

### 1. You say what the business is

One sentence is enough. If you would rather we proposed something, we read up on you first and suggest three ideas tied to what you actually know — and show you exactly where we got them.

### 2. It works while you are gone

Your company gets a live address, its own inbox, and somewhere to put code the same night. Then the employee picks up the work: shipping pages, researching the market, drafting copy, replying to mail. Anything that spends money or goes public waits for you.

### 3. You read one page in the morning

What shipped, what it learned, and the single question it needs answered to keep moving. Answer in one tap and tonight's shift starts from there.

## Every action leaves a receipt

The most common complaint about autonomous AI products is that you cannot tell whether the work happened. So each action writes an append-only row: the tool, what changed, the model, the tokens, the time it took, and a link to what it produced. Export it whenever you like.

Note row five: sending mail is held for approval — nothing goes out until you say so.

## You keep custody of your money

The best-known product in this category collects your customers' payments into a balance it controls, keeps 20% of every one, holds the rest for two weeks, and then caps how much you may withdraw in a calendar month. It also takes 20% off the top of your ad budget, so a fifth of what you meant to spend on advertising never becomes advertising.

We are not free — the managed plan takes 15% of what your company earns, and 15% to run your ad campaigns. The difference is where the money sits. Your customer pays into your own Stripe account and Stripe settles our share at the transaction, so we never hold a balance and could not cap your withdrawals if we tried. And because our advertising fee is charged on top rather than skimmed off, your whole ad budget buys ads.
